edges.effect_quant: The strongest quantitative studies point in a harmful direction, but the pooled magnitude varies across populations and methods.
edges.mechanism: Atrial fibrillation may promote dementia through embolic injury, reduced cerebral perfusion, and shared vascular disease rather than through one isolated stroke alone.
edges.summary: For dementia (all-cause), the most useful starting point is the 2026 Sagaro meta analysis in Int J Mol Sci. It found that atrial fibrillation tracks with higher risk or worse outcomes, and the follow-on evidence is broadly consistent even when absolute benefit or harm is modest.
edges.caveats: Residual confounding and reverse causation remain possible in some observational studies, so the main readout is direction and plausibility rather than one exact risk number.
